stem.en: Magadha gradually became the most powerful of the sixteen mahājanapadas. Which set of reasons accounts for this?

text.en: It was the first of the sixteen to be founded, so it had the longest time to grow.
It had fertile plains, and no other reason was needed.
It had a strategic location, fertile plains and strong rulers.
It lay in the far north-west, close to the early centres of Vedic culture.

explanation.en: Three reasons are given: strategic location, fertile plains and strong rulers. Together they let Magadha expand its control over neighbouring regions, which led in time to the Mauryan Empire.

hints.en: One reason is about place, one about the soil, and one about people.
Magadha lay in present-day Bihar, far from the north-west.
